extracted.intended_audience: students and teachers of English/poetry learning practical criticism
extracted.subtask_description: Close-reading and critical evaluation of lyric poems for classroom instruction, emphasising detailed observation of form, sound, sense, and reader-response. Focuses on what to attend to and common faults readers/poets show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe matter and manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Detailed observation of the matter and manner of the poem.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criticism seeks observations of both what the poem says (matter) and how it says it (manner). Pair suspicions or impressions with concrete details about language, rhythm, imagery, and structure rather than relying on vague impressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware sentimentality / cheap reassurance
rubrics_metrics.description: Poems that 'play for easily touched off and full-volumed responses' are in danger of sentimentality and kindred vices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify vacuous resonances and unctuous poetic manner (e.g. 'its essential self in its own season') as anti-patterns. Ask whether emotion is genuinely earned or merely produced by familiar rhetorical devices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Detect imitation and poetic indebtedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice echoes and mannerisms of other poets (e.g. 'Browning', 'Wordsworth', 'Marvell') that shape a poem's tone and effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the poem is distinctive or a pastiche ('Shakespeare-R. Brooke' complex). Excessive indebtedness, imitation, or forced allusion may weaken imaginative integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity vs obscurity (comprehension)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the poem is clear or obscure; if it 'requires a special reading' or is 'difficult to understand at first.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish genuine obscurity from complexity that rewards repeated readings. Note when readers attend more to sound than sense, or when a poem's meaning only emerges after multiple 'attacks' (readings). Consider if obscurity is integral to the poem or a failure of expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sound, rhythm and rhyme (musical qualities)
rubrics_metrics.description: Sound-patterns—alliteration, vowel music, rhyme, meter, and general word-pattern—are central to a poem's effect ('balanced alliterative rhythm and rhyme scheme').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how sound contributes to meaning: vowel choices, triple rhymes, 'breathing sigh' phrasing, and the interweaving of sound and sense. Beware when focus on sound causes neglect of sense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accentuation, tempo and breathing
rubrics_metrics.description: Accent placement and tempo (e.g. stress on 'will' vs 'weep' altering sense and rhythm) critically affect meaning.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examine marks of accent, suggested pauses or gaps in lines ('And yet you will weep (gap) and know why') and prescribe appropriate speed/tempo. Note that small accentual shifts can produce wholly different readings and meanings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Metre and scannability
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence and regularity of metrical scheme; ease of scansion ('There doesn't seem to be the least vestige of a metrical scheme' is a fault).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check whether metre supports the poem's mood and whether lines can be scanned; lack of a discernible meter may impede reading and be counted as a weakness unless deliberate and effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form fits content / structural appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The formal structure should suit the subject matter (e.g. 'The form fits the contents to perfection'; sonnet-like bipartite structure, framing couplets that functionally frame the argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate symmetry, framing, and overall architecture (couplets, segments) and whether they clarify or illuminate the poem's argument/feeling. Consider whether formal economy and structure intensify rather than dilute meaning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compression and economy of expression
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of compression (e.g. 'means of compression', 'freedom of words' leading to 'newness') to make expression concentrated and universal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Praise judicious compression and coinages that lend distinction, and note when compression becomes cramping or obscures meaning. Assess whether lack of particularising detail creates universal appeal or vagueness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality versus particularising detail
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance between universal application and particularising strokes that ground the poem ('not the least particularising detail... yet subtle strokes like "Golden grove," "Margaret"').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether specificity removes 'airy nothing' and gives the poem individuality while allowing universal resonance; too little particularity may yield vagueness, too much may localise the effect unfairly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Imagery and the pathetic fallacy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of imagery and attribution of feeling to nature (pathetic fallacy) can be powerful or overworked ('The trees don't worship, arise, or run').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge whether personification serves a valid poetic argument or is an overworked device that becomes blatantly false. Consider whether such images function as argument or ornament and whether they are overinsistent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sincerity and imaginative integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the poem's shaping motive is sincere or shows failure of imaginative integrity (false simplicity, exaggeration, strained expression).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate crude insincerity (conscious affectation) from subtler failures where the poet cannot distinguish genuine promptings from effects he hopes to produce. Signs: strained expression, indebtedness to other poetry, exaggerated or forced phrasing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expression vs content balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether expression (style, diction, technique) aligns with and supports the poem's ideas, or whether style misdirects energy from sense ('experiment in sound ... the sense suffers').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch for experiments in sound or manner that obscure meaning; assess if technical devices justify their cost in clarity and argumentative force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Choice of words and diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Diction choices ('so meet a place', 'sacramental', coinages like 'wanwood') affect tone and reader reaction; smug or self-conscious word choice can repel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate word choice for clarity, appropriateness, connotation, and possible archaisms or neologisms that confuse. Note when diction creates a 'smugness' or self-consciousness that undermines the poem.

rubrics_metrics.name: Coherence, logic and unity
rubrics_metrics.description: Connectedness of thought, presence of trite or dropped lines, and whether the poem's parts hold together as an argument or mood ('disconnected and rather pointless', 'an extra line seems to have dropped into the middle').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess structural and logical unity; identify accidental insertions, muddled transitions, or triteness. A poem should avoid being merely a jumble of half-evolved thoughts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional communication and authenticity of feeling
rubrics_metrics.description: Power of the poem to convey authentic emotion (e.g. 'poignant', 'perfect melancholy') versus provoking mere derision or annoyance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note genuine emotional conveyance (that which 'sticks in the throat like real sorrow') and distinguish it from sentimental or artificial effects which provoke contempt or laughter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intrusive or accidental images (ludicrousness risk)
rubrics_metrics.description: Precise images that spontaneously evoke ludicrous associations can distract ('a forward breaking away with the ball...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Determine whether accidental literal images undermine the intended seriousness. A precise but incongruous image may be tolerated but multiple instances suggest a tendency toward the ludicrous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical skill used toward trivial ends
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical perfection used to express common or trivial sentiments ('technical perfection to express a common human jailing') can be misapplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether technical mastery enriches content or merely gilds trite ideas. Praise technique when it amplifies thought; be critical when it masks emptiness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reader bias and doctrinal prejudices
rubrics_metrics.description: Critical judgement is often affected by doctrinal 'bees' (prejudices) which must be deliberately set aside.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware of critics' traditional/advanced biases and how they may colour judgments (e.g. hostility to prayer or mysticism). Strive to isolate poem-specific evidence rather than ideological reactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiplicity of legitimate readings
rubrics_metrics.description: A poem may legitimately allow more than one reading (e.g. alternative accentuation leads to distinct senses); critics should note and weigh alternate readings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Record possible readings and how performative choices (accent, pause, tempo) change meaning. Treat alternative readings as part of the poem's texture rather than mere error, and consider which reading the poet seems to authorize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of local details to overall movement
rubrics_metrics.description: How local rhythms, lilt-breakers, and grouped lines contribute to the poem's larger progression and climactic fusion ('lilt-breaker (l.7)', 'fusion in the last 2 lines').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyse how small formal moves (line-grouping, local rhythm changes) prepare or contrast the poem's culminating effect. Pay attention to how 'whole' and 'local' rhythms interact to build meaning.
